text:
- chief complaint: the patient reports months of worsening headaches and was referred after an incidental pituitary lesion was found.
- history of present illness: about three months of progressively worsening, dull headaches behind the eyes, now 6/10, worse in the morning and lasting hours. Recently the patient has been bumping into door frames. No prior headache history, no past medical history, no medications, no alcohol, smoking, or drug use. MRI shows a pituitary lesion compressing the optic chiasm.
- physical examination: alert and oriented, fluent speech, cranial nerves grossly intact, no focal motor or sensory deficits, normal visual acuity and eye movements, pupils equal and reactive, bitemporal hemianopia, normal color vision.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: retro-orbital headaches, worsening over time, and bumping into door frames. Denies nausea, fever, rash, neck stiffness, numbness, tingling, weakness, syncope, or noticed vision change.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: N/A.
- follow-up instructions: ophthalmology referral for visual field testing before surgery, then post-operative vision monitoring. Transsphenoidal surgery to excise the adenoma and decompress the chiasm, with the surgery scheduler arranging the date.
